"FLORIDA 300X THE CASH" has gone five months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. Most of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $15 million prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

Every line of FLORIDA 300X THE CASH's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
5048.headline: Good news: no big claims

5055.body:
"EMERALD MINE 9X" is in the last part of its run, with only a small slice of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

Every line of EMERALD MINE 9X's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
5055.headline: How far along this game is

5057.body:
The most common win left on "EASY MONEY" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and two of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Today's free summary of "EASY MONEY" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
5057.headline: A close look at the prizes

5059.body:
"THE CASH WHEEL" has had no $1 million top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Everything above about "THE CASH WHEEL" comes from the Florida Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
5059.headline: No top prize claimed lately

5060.body:
The most common win left on "FIND THE 7S" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $500, and 47 of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If "FIND THE 7S" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
5060.headline: Prize table details

5063.body:
"CA$H IN HAND" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $2 million was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold two of the original four. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

Everything here about "CA$H IN HAND" comes from official Florida lottery numbers, current through November 8.
5063.headline: The top prize list got shorter
